title: Schedule of Breakage and Reinstatement Terms for Payment Arrangements
content:
Each type of Payment Arrangements carries four breakage and reinstatement terms: the number of uncured missed installments at which the plan is broken; the calendar days after a plan breaks within which it may be reinstated (0 meaning it cannot be); the largest number of reinstatements over the life of the plan; and what must be paid to reinstate.

| Arrangement type | Uncured misses that break the plan | Reinstatement window (calendar days) | Reinstatements over the plan's life | Cure required to reinstate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Promise-to-Pay Arrangement | 1 | 0 | 0 | Not reinstatable |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | 2 | 15 | 1 | All missed installments |
| Standard Installment Plan | 2 | 30 | 2 | All missed installments |
| Extended Installment Plan | 2 | 30 | 2 | All missed installments |
| Long-Term Installment Plan | 2 | 30 | 2 | One installment |
| Hardship Reduced-Payment Plan | 3 | 45 | 3 | One installment |

## The cure terms

- **Not reinstatable** — the type allows no reinstatement; its window and its reinstatement count both read 0.
- **All missed installments** — every missed installment must be paid in full.
- **One installment** — one full regular installment must be paid after the break.

## Observations drawn from the schedule

- A Promise-to-Pay Arrangement is broken by its first uncured missed installment and cannot be reinstated.
- The Hardship Reduced-Payment Plan tolerates the most: it breaks at 3 uncured misses, keeps a 45-day window and allows up to 3 reinstatements.
- A Short-Term Installment Plan may be reinstated once over its life; a Standard, Extended or Long-Term Installment Plan twice.
